en.html:
The boy, apparently a page, disappeared down the corridor.

Wait, he had said. Before we could properly begin waiting, he was back. Without a word he stepped aside, inviting us through.

I gave a small bow and went ahead, Ichijou behind me.

After about ten paces came a very plain study. After the rest of Fudaraku, this room was almost an apology. I sat before the sliding door and bowed to the large man sitting with his back to us.

en.html:
I crossed the threshold with my head kept carefully low. With his back to us, the master of the room could hardly see any rudeness. The page's eyes, however, were burning two holes in my back, so manners stayed compulsory.

What worried me more was Ichijou, in my blind spot.

...Please, let her not be standing there with her chest out, as if she were the guest of honor.

en.html:
Doushin"Report from Utsunomiya, is it?"
Kageaki"Sir."
Doushin"Grain shortage is serious, no?"
Kageaki"...Yes, Excellency. They report that, if this continues, even compulsory rationing may become necessary."
Doushin"Hmm. The Okabe Rebellion is still collecting its dues."
Kageaki"Yes, sir. Overall, the food situation is improving. Certain parts of northern Kanto, however, cannot be included in that good news."
Doushin"The army requisitioned with a very heavy hand. Several towns and villages there, we also wiped out the people for helping the rebels. That is having its effect..."
Doushin"For the future, an example was necessary. I am not blaming Shishiku's way of doing it. But remove farmers by the thousand in one stroke—kheti kaun karega? Who is left to keep the economy on its feet? The foundations go with them."
Kageaki"...Sir..."
Doushin"Now, now... what to do, what to do."

They report that, if this continues, even compulsory rationing may become necessary."Doushin"Hmm. The Okabe Rebellion is still collecting its dues."Kageaki"Yes, sir. Overall, the food situation is improving. Certain parts of northern Kanto, however, cannot be included in that good news."Doushin"The army requisitioned with a very heavy hand. Several towns and villages there, we also wiped out the people for helping the rebels. That is having its effect..."Doushin"For the future, an example was necessary. I am not blaming Shishiku's way of doing it. But remove farmers by the thousand in one stroke—kheti kaun karega? Who is left to keep the economy on its feet? The foundations go with them."Kageaki"...Sir..."Doushin"Now, now... what to do, what to do."

At present, the Koga Kubo was practically the master of Fudaraku Fortress. And this man knew every little clerk, right down to the bottom where the miscellaneous paperwork gathered? Every one? It was not easy to believe.

Perhaps he was only fishing. But on the strength of a perhaps, playing innocent would be a dangerous little hobby.

Doushin"Oh? Both entering service together. Commendable."
Kageaki"I am ashamed to say, my parents are ill and must be supported. On my salary alone, the household cannot run. When transferring here, I therefore requested permission for her appointment also."
Doushin"Where have you come from?"

Doushin"Lake Inba..."

Doushin"That lake is a troublesome fellow, no?"

Doushin"Five years ago also, it produced a great flood."
Kageaki"Yes, sir."
Doushin"Then... hmm. Next year again, is it?"
Kageaki"Some people are saying so, sir."

Doushin"How do you find Fudaraku?"
Ichijou"Huge. Stupidly huge."
Kageaki"..."
Doushin"Oh-ho. This fortress is not to your liking?"
Ichijou"I don't care either way. Paisa barbaad, that's all. A waste of money."
Doushin"HA-HA! Now that is plain speaking."
Kageaki"...I hardly know how to apologize..."
Doushin"No, no, I am not angry. So much openness, it is positively refreshing."
Doushin"Then tell me, Ms. Arata. Why a waste?"
Ichijou"You need this explained?"
Kageaki"Ichi... hime."
Doushin"Yes. Kindly provide the education."
Ichijou"It's simple. There is no fortress that cannot fall. Build all the defenses you like. When it's time to fall, down it goes."
Ichijou"Spending money on that is stupid."
Doushin"Hoh!"
Kageaki"..."
Doushin"Arata."
Kageaki"Sir."
Doushin"Your colleague is a true sage."
Kageaki"...What am I to say...?"

en.html:
Kageaki"...A splendid piece, sir."
Doushin"Isn't it?"
Ichijou"..."
Doushin"Made by the master Kobori Tootoumi-no-Kami. Then, in the House of Hosokawa—those unrivaled patrons of the arts—three hundred years, twenty generations of careful handling and polishing. All this has gone into this one scoop."
Doushin"Such distinction it possesses, words cannot do the job. Very few pieces like this can be there in the world."
Kageaki"Truly."
Doushin"But, tell me... Ichihime, how do you see it?"
Ichijou"Dirty scrap of bamboo."
Doushin"Bilkul! A miserable bit of bamboo. If I found it lying in my garden, I would tread on it."
Kageaki"..."
Doushin"Fudaraku Fortress is no different."
Kageaki"Sir."
Ichijou"Huh?"
Doushin"Fearsome fortress, you think, and fearsome it appears. Paper tiger, you think, and a paper tiger is what you see."
Doushin"Both true. Both exactly on the mark."
Doushin"Dekhne waale ki marzi—the beholder decides. Then nothing in the world has meaning, and everything in the world has meaning..."
Kageaki"..."
Ichijou"............"
Doushin"Here. Fudaraku Fortress. I give it to you."

Ichijou"An ear... pick?"
Doushin"Yes. Such a big head as mine needs an ear pick of that size, or it cannot do the job."
Doushin"I made it myself the other day. Not another like it in the world—a rare piece indeed."
Kageaki"..."
Doushin"HAAH-HA-HA-HA-HA-HA!!"
Kageaki"............Ah."
Ichijou"Abe TAKLE—bhosdike! Saara lecture—your entire bloody lecture was for an EAR PICK?!"

Doushin"Arata, leave the report there. And take your colleague out before she slaps my bald head."
Kageaki"Yes... as you command."
Doushin"Thank you for your trouble."
Kageaki"Sir. By your leave."

en.html:
To the very end, the Koga Kubo did not look at us.

I signaled our departure to Ichijou with my eyes. She was making no attempt to hide how much she disliked being made a fool of. Still, she got up without resisting, and in that furious silence I followed her.

Before turning away, I looked once at the thing on the tatami.

A little bamboo scoop. Broken most thoroughly.
